Matt — thanks for the diagram and checklist. Quick read-through below; I copied Priyom and Irene for the handoff notes. Long story short: we recommend a management VLAN for the Redwood control-plane components and a separate data VLAN for inference lanes. Reasoning and action items below: 

- Control plane on management VLAN:
  - Pros: stronger audit boundary (saves you from mixing tenant data plane traffic with control plane telemetry), easier to integrate with customer KMS and HSM via the management plane, and simpler cert distribution.
  - Cons: adds one extra hop to data-plane worker registration — latency impact is negligible for our control traffic since control messages are small and infrequent.

- PXE / provisioning NAT: we recommend using your edge router for outbound NAT during PXE. That keeps boot images pulled through your colo egress (helps with IP allowlists) and avoids needing host-level SNAT changes in the provisioning image.

- Egress/proxy: for compliance (you mentioned PCI-scoped workloads), put an egress proxy in front of the management VLAN with request-level logging forwarded to your audit cluster. Redwood can send our control-plane logs to a dedicated forwarding endpoint (TLS) if you prefer not to store them locally.

Action items (short):
1) Priya to share a small annotated SVG showing demarc lines for control/data VLANs (will attach by EOD).
2) Priyom to propose a minimal firewall ACL set (ports and CIDRs) for the management VLAN.
3) Jonas to validate certificate rotation path and KMS endpoints (Irene will help on the ops runbook).

We can go deeper in a 30m call; propose Monday Sep 6 10am PT if that still matches your provisioning window.

—Priya

On Mon, Aug 23, 2026 at 11:05 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Matt — thanks for the diagram and checklist. Quick read-through below; I copied Priyom and Irene for the handoff notes. Long story short: we recommend a management VLAN for the Redwood control-plane components and a separate data VLAN for inference lanes. Reasoning and action items below:

Couple of practical notes from the ops side:

- Firewall/ACLs (minimal) we need:
  - Management VLAN -> Redwood Control IPs: TCP 443, 8443 (control plane API), 5222 (agent bootstrap), 123 (NTP)
  - Data VLAN -> Public egress (for model fetches): TCP 443 outbound only; prefer prefix-list so we can avoid IP churn.
  - BGP sessions: if you're peering, allow TCP 179 between your edge and the Redwood transit peer.

- PXE: confirm your DHCP boot options will not block HTTP(S); we often rely on HTTP(s) to fetch images. If the colo provides a RFC-compliant DHCP, the edge NAT approach Priya proposed works cleanly.

- Provisioning order (recommended):
  1) Prepare management VLAN + ACLs
  2) Deploy control-plane nodes on management VLAN (init certs via KMS endpoint)
  3) Run agent registration from data VLAN (agents authenticate to control-plane through the management VLAN hop)
  4) Canary: 2 host-level workers pinned to a dedicated tenant pool for smoke load

I attached a quick checklist (provisioning-checklist.csv) and added a column with the CIDR/port rows I suggest.

--Priyom

Matt — following up after the internal lab run we did yesterday. A few clarifications and a short canary playbook so the on-site team has repeatable steps: 

Canary playbook (short):
- Goal: get two worker hosts carrying a synthetic tenant traffic profile, validate model pull, KV cache warm, and verify KMS attestation.
- Preconditions: management VLAN up, control-plane certs loaded via your KMS endpoint, ACLs applied per Priyom's CSV.
- Steps:
  1) PXE boot hosts with the Redwood provisioning image (verify HTTP(S) fetch through edge NAT).
  2) Start control-plane pods on management VLAN; confirm /health and /metrics endpoints.
  3) Run agent registration script (we'll provide a signed token) from data VLAN hosts; ensure they register and appear in the control-plane UI.
  4) Deploy a tiny model (50MB) to the canary worker pool, run 1k requests across both hosts, measure p50/p95 latency and egress throughput.
  5) Validate cert rotation path: rotate signing key in staging KMS and confirm agents re-establish TLS without manual intervention.

Rollback: if registration fails or agent auth errors, quarantine affected hosts (block their ACL) and call the on-call ops line we’ll share.

We also sketched a demarc SVG (Drive link above) that highlights MACsec-capable links and where we'd prefer to terminate GRE if you need a transparent control overlay. Priya — I grabbed the diagram you promised and annotated the BGP community tags for your edge team.

If that all looks good, let's lock Sep 6 10am PT for the on-site provisioning and I’ll create a short runbook artifact (INFRA-1129) with the checklist embedded.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
